title: Client Enablement & Coaching Lead (F/H/X)
description: Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe! Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy. We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide. It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone. What we do: build the most AI-driven, innovative, forward-thinking platform for energy management. From optimizing resources to delivering cost-effective, exceptional customer experiences through advanced Customer Information Systems (CIS), billing, meter data management, CRM, and AI-driven communications, Kraken is powering the next wave of innovation in the energy industry. Why we do it: future energy will not look like energy as we know it today. We need to not just think about our future, but build for it. Now. You will play a key role in delivering Kraken's Human Design principles and Operating Model to transform our clients Operations, leading implementation through a hands-on, consultative approach. A strong understanding of Human Design principles and change management best practice is essential, as is the ability to influence leaders, navigate change with confidence and bring sharp project management and analytical skills. You are responsible for guiding clients through the Kraken migration framework (BOT method), mentoring internal and external stakeholders, and ensuring operational success and long-term sustainability of the target operating model. While operations will be your core focus, you’ll also need a solid grasp of broader retail functions – how data, comms and marketing interact with operations to shape customer outcomes and influence the success of the new model. While the primary focus is the C&I function, you’ll also need B2C experience to effectively support clients across the portfolio. When executed well, these transformations can feel truly magical – across the whole organisation, and most importantly, our clients’ customers. The SCDL role is to make sure that magic is felt. Key Responsibilities: what you'll do Consultative Leadership & Client Engagement: Lead client interactions through the entire BOT program lifecycle, providing hands-on consulting and fostering a learning environment by guiding clients to take ownership early in the migration process of the operational programme. Help mobilise and set up initiatives such as Operations Transformation Office (OTO - client’s internal change management team), Early Adopters and work closely with Kraken’s Tech Teams to enable a smooth transformation. Establish strong relationships within the client’s Senior Leadership team, acting as a trusted advisor and helping to shape, influence and unblock strategic decisions. Empower the client’s migration ‘Ambassadors’ to become champions of the model, ensuring the program’s long term adoption and accountability across the organisation. Shape planning so it aligns with the client’s goals and aspirations. Project Management: Guide the delivery of Kraken programmes – from Leadership Development to Skills Based Learning – by defining clear programme milestones that keep teams and stakeholders on track and organised. Partner tightly with internal Tech teams so operational and technical migrations run in lockstep, reducing friction and keeping delivery on track. Drive continuous improvement and iteration, tailoring solutions based on client-specific needs. Mentorship & Coaching: Cultivate future leadership by mentoring and coaching the client’s OTO and internal teams, enabling them to be successful in a Kraken powered organisation. Ensure that internal stakeholders, including the OTO team, are fully equipped to take over ownership of scaling the operational transformation, with formalised check-ins at agreed points. Support the creation of high performing teams, able to think, lead and problem solve and lead in keeping with agile, customer centric methodologies. Analytical & Problem-Solving: Utilise strong analytical skills to anticipate challenges, pre-empt pain points and intervene early on to course correct. Leverage client and Kraken data to identify red flags, understand cause-and-effect relationships, and drive corrective actions to improve client outcomes. Being able to correlate and articulate the connection between employee engagement and customer satisfaction, and how operational changes can impact cost to serve. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Influence: Collaborate with multiple teams and stakeholders both within Kraken and across client internal teams such as HR, Data, Marketing and Tech to provide clear guidance on program delivery and solutions while managing client expectations. Collaborate across departments to ensure that Kraken’s core offering aligns with client expectations. Ensure that operations never become a blocker to continued migration. Remain up to date with new features and products and ensure the client is trained and adopts new functionality. Driving Organisational Change: Lead cultural and operational transformations, embedding sustainable change within the client’s organisation, using Kraken’s Human Design approach. Champion the Kraken Operating model, ensuring the client’s operational structure evolves in alignment with best practices for both immediate and long-term success. Skills: what you'll have Exceptional project management skills, with the ability to work across multiple clients and fast-paced timelines. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify risks, and proactively implement solutions. Proven influencing skills, with experience persuading senior leaders and driving adoption of new methodologies. Deep technical understanding of Kraken's products and services, including migration processes and temporary solutions. Demonstrating leadership practices and promoting professionalism in client interactions Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to explain complex concepts and principles to a varied audience. Fluent English & French is a prerequisite Experience Proven communication at all levels, able to leverage style at Exec level. Exposure to outsourcing models (BPOs), understanding their drivers, challenges, and how to manage these relationships effectively. Change management using agile methodologies. Proven record of creating high performing teams, either internally within operations or externally with clients. Other Requirements: Ability to travel globally, with placement based on preference when possible, but flexibility required according to client needs. Ability to work across multiple clients and markets, quickly adapting to varying client needs and environments/languages. Highly driven to ‘make things happen’. Growth mindset demonstrated through all your work. Ability to speak persuasively and inspire energy, motivating both internal teams and external stakeholders including Direct Reports. Comfortable navigating between operations and technical conversations, bridging gaps between business needs and technical solutions. Expertise in driving programme ownership, from inception through to sustainable execution, ensuring clients are equipped to lead post-migration. raw.title: Client Enablement & Coaching Lead (f/m/d) - Dutch & German speaking
raw.description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

What we do: build the most AI-driven, innovative, forward-thinking platform for energy management. From optimizing resources to delivering cost-effective, exceptional customer experiences through advanced Customer Information Systems (CIS), billing, meter data management, CRM, and AI-driven communications, Kraken is powering the next wave of innovation in the energy industry.

 

Why we do it: future energy will not look like energy as we know it today. We need to not just think about our future, but build for it. Now.

 

You will play a key role in delivering Kraken's Human Design principles and Operating Model to transform our clients Operations, leading implementation through a hands-on, consultative approach. A strong understanding of Human Design principles and change management best practice is essential, as is the ability to influence leaders, navigate change with confidence and bring sharp project management and analytical skills.

 

You are responsible for guiding clients through the Kraken migration framework (BOT method), mentoring internal and external stakeholders, and ensuring operational success and long-term sustainability of the target operating model. 

 

While operations will be your core focus, you’ll also need a solid grasp of broader retail functions – how data, comms and marketing interact with operations to shape customer outcomes and influence the success of the new model. While the primary focus is the C&I function, you’ll also need B2C experience to effectively support clients across the portfolio.

 

When executed well, these transformations can feel truly magical – across the whole organisation, and most importantly, our clients’ customers. The SCDL role is to make sure that magic is felt.

Key Responsibilities: what you'll do

  • Consultative Leadership & Client Engagement:

  • Lead client interactions through the entire BOT program lifecycle, providing hands-on consulting and fostering a learning environment by guiding clients to take ownership early in the migration process of the operational programme.

  • Help mobilise and set up initiatives such as Operations Transformation Office (OTO - client’s internal change management team), Early Adopters and work closely with Kraken’s Tech Teams to enable a smooth transformation.

  • Establish strong relationships within the client’s Senior Leadership team, acting as a trusted advisor and helping to shape, influence and unblock strategic decisions.

  • Empower the client’s migration ‘Ambassadors’ to become champions of the model, ensuring the program’s long term adoption and accountability across the organisation.

  • Shape planning so it aligns with the client’s goals and aspirations.

 

Project Management:

  • Guide the delivery of Kraken programmes – from Leadership Development to Skills Based Learning – by defining clear programme milestones that keep teams and stakeholders on track and organised.

  • Partner tightly with internal Tech teams so operational and technical migrations run in lockstep, reducing friction and keeping delivery on track.

  • Drive continuous improvement and iteration, tailoring solutions based on client-specific needs.

 

Mentorship & Coaching:

  • Cultivate future leadership by mentoring and coaching the client’s OTO and internal teams, enabling them to be successful in a Kraken powered organisation.

  • Ensure that internal stakeholders, including the OTO team, are fully equipped to take over ownership of scaling the operational transformation, with formalised check-ins at agreed points. Support the creation of high performing teams, able to think, lead and problem solve and lead in keeping with agile, customer centric methodologies.

 

Analytical & Problem-Solving:

  • Utilise strong analytical skills to anticipate challenges, pre-empt pain points and intervene early on to course correct.

  • Leverage client and Kraken data to identify red flags, understand cause-and-effect relationships, and drive corrective actions to improve client outcomes.

  • Being able to correlate and articulate the connection between employee engagement and customer satisfaction, and how operational changes can impact cost to serve.

 

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Influence:

  • Collaborate with multiple teams and stakeholders both within Kraken and across client internal teams such as HR, Data, Marketing and  Tech to provide clear guidance on program delivery and solutions while managing client expectations.

  • Collaborate across departments to ensure that Kraken’s core offering aligns with client expectations. Ensure that operations never become a blocker to continued migration.

  • Remain up to date with new features and products and ensure the client is trained and adopts new functionality.

 

Driving Organisational Change:

  • Lead cultural and operational transformations, embedding sustainable change within the client’s organisation, using Kraken’s Human Design approach.

  • Champion the Kraken Operating model, ensuring the client’s operational structure evolves in alignment with best practices for both immediate and long-term success.

Skills: what you'll have

  • Exceptional project management skills, with the ability to work across multiple clients and fast-paced timelines.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify risks, and proactively implement solutions.

  • Proven influencing skills, with experience persuading senior leaders and driving adoption of new methodologies.

  • Deep technical understanding of Kraken's products and services, including migration processes and temporary solutions.

  • Demonstrating leadership practices and promoting professionalism in client interactions Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to explain complex concepts and principles to a varied audience.

 

Experience

  • Proven communication at all levels, able to leverage style at Exec level.

  • Exposure to outsourcing models (BPOs), understanding their drivers, challenges, and how to manage these relationships effectively.

  • Change management using agile methodologies.

  • Proven record of creating high performing teams, either internally within operations or externally with clients. 

 

Other Requirements:

  • Ability to travel globally, with placement based on preference when possible, but flexibility required according to client needs.

  • Ability to work across multiple clients and markets, quickly adapting to varying client needs and environments/languages.

  • Highly driven to ‘make things happen’. Growth mindset demonstrated through all your work. Ability to speak persuasively and inspire energy, motivating both internal teams and external stakeholders including Direct Reports.

  • Comfortable navigating between operations and technical conversations, bridging gaps between business needs and technical solutions.

  • Expertise in driving programme ownership, from inception through to sustainable execution, ensuring clients are equipped to lead post-migration.

  • Fluent German & Dutch is a prerequisite for this role

Please submit your resume in English 🇬🇧

This position involves travelling across different European countries 🚃

title: Marketing Associate – Special Projects & Events
description: Marketing Associate – Special Projects & Events Festanstellung · Vollzeit · Berlin (HQ) Unsere Mission für dich Du baust den Kanal, über den trawa dem industriellen Mittelstand begegnet: mehr als 30 Messen, Kongresse und Roundtables im Jahr, von der fünftägigen Leitmesse bis zum Fachkongress auf sechs Quadratmetern. Du entscheidest mit, welche davon stattfinden, führst sie durch und stehst für das Ergebnis ein. Es bleibt nicht beim Stand. Du baust die Landingpage, bewirbst die Events in Paid und Content und schreibst den LinkedIn-Post zur Messewoche. In kurzer Zeit kennst du den kompletten Weg von der Standfläche bis zur Opportunity im CRM — eine Breite, die dir ein großes Marketingteam nicht bietet. Europas B2B-Sektor gibt jährlich über 200 Milliarden Euro für Energie aus. Die Zeit, diesen Markt zu dekarbonisieren und unsere Markenbekanntheit zu steigern, ist jetzt. Das Team Neben dir sitzen Content, Growth und Product Marketing — Events sind der Kanal, an dem alle drei zusammenlaufen. Gleichzeitig bist du näher an Sales als die meisten Marketingrollen. Auf jeder Messe stehen Seller mit am Stand, und der Wert eines Events entsteht erst, wenn aus Gesprächen Termine werden. Du stimmst dich laufend mit Sales, SDRs und Revenue Operations ab. Deine Aufgaben Du ownst den Eventkalender. Welche Messe, welches Format, welches Budget. Du planst das Jahr, rechnest jedes Event durch und sagst ab, wenn die Zahl nicht stimmt. Du baust den Auftritt. Standfläche, Standbau, Grafik, Technik, Logistik. Du verhandelst mit Messegesellschaften und Dienstleistern, hältst die Fristen ein und stehst vor Ort selbst am Stand. Du machst aus Standtagen Termine. Einladungskampagnen, Teilnehmerlisten, Matchmaking, Terminsetzung vorab. Danach: Lead-Erfassung, Nachfass und Übergabe an Sales entlang eines klaren SLA. Du misst deine eigene Arbeit. Landingpages, Formulare, HubSpot-Workflows, Lead-Tagging und Reporting baust du selbst — und berichtest MQLs, Pipeline und Signings je Event gegen Plan. Du bleibst nicht bei Events. Newsletter, LinkedIn, PR und eigene Formate gehören dazu, bis hin zu Guerilla-Experimenten wie Briefkampagnen oder OOH. Was funktioniert, wiederholen wir. Nach wem wir suchen Ein bis vier Jahre B2B-Marketing mit Schwerpunkt Events oder Messen, gern mit Bezug zum deutschen Mittelstand Du bist extrovertiert: Auf dem Stand gehst du auf Menschen zu, statt zu warten, bis jemand stehen bleibt. Viele Gespräche am Tag geben dir Energie Du behältst den Überblick, wenn ein Dutzend Dienstleister und mehrere Messen parallel laufen – und eskalierst rechtzeitig Du denkst kaufmännisch und bewertest ein Event an dem, was es an Pipeline bringt Du baust dir Landingpage, Formular und Reporting selbst Bias to Action: lieber schnell testen und messen als lange konzipieren Deutsch muttersprachlich, gutes Englisch Berlin oder Umzug dorthin, plus Reisebereitschaft in der Messesaison und einen Führerschein Deine ersten 90 Tage: Nach sechs Wochen: Onboarding Du hast trawas Geschäftsmodell, Produkt und Zielgruppe im Detail verstanden und alle relevanten Stakeholder in Marketing und Sales kennengelernt. Du hast das laufende Eventportfolio übernommen, kennst jeden offenen Punkt und jede Frist und hast die Abläufe dokumentiert. Du warst auf allen Messen vor Ort, die in dieser Zeit stattfanden, und hast konkrete Verbesserungen benannt und erste Verantwortung übernommen. Im dritten Monat: Ramp-up Du verantwortest eigene Key Results im neuen Planungszyklus und lässt dich an den erzielten Ergebnissen messen. Du hast die Planung für das kommende Halbjahr aufgesetzt, jedes Event durchgerechnet und einen Entscheidungsvorschlag vorgelegt. Ein wiederverwendbarer Ablauf steht: Vorlauf, Aktivierung, Lead-Erfassung, Nachfass — nachvollziehbar genug, dass jemand anderes ihn ausführen könnte.. Warum wir? Gestalte mit uns die Zukunft der Energiewirtschaft und treibe eigenverantwortlich Projekte voran, die echten Einfluss auf unsere Produkte, unsere Kund:innen und die Umwelt haben. Dein Impact: Jede Messe bringt uns mit Unternehmen zusammen, deren Energiekosten wir senken und deren Verbrauch wir dekarbonisieren. Gestaltungsspielraum: Das Event-Marketing bei trawa ist im Aufbau. Du erbst keine fertigen Strukturen, sondern etablierst sie. Flexibles Arbeiten: Dich erwartet ein schönes Büro in Berlin mit einer lebendigen Unternehmenskultur. Homeoffice und flexible Arbeitszeiten sind möglich, 30 Urlaubstage unterstützen deine Work-Life-Balance. Attraktive Benefits: Neben einem wettbewerbsfähigen Gehalt erhältst du Essensgutscheine, eine Urban-Sports-Mitgliedschaft, reichlich kostenlose Snacks und ein persönliches Weiterbildungsbudget. Persönliche Entwicklung: Weiterbildungstage, ein jährliches L&D-Budget und Coaching-Sessions über Sparrks. Vielfalt und Inklusion: Bei uns sind alle willkommen. Wir setzen uns für einen inklusiven Arbeitsplatz ein, der Vielfalt wertschätzt, und ermutigen Menschen unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, sexueller Orientierung, ethnischer und sozialer Herkunft sowie körperlicher oder neurodiverser Vielfalt zur Bewerbung. Wenn du strategisch denkst, operativ stark bist und gerne Verantwortung übernimmst, dann bewirb dich jetzt! Auch wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen zu 100 % erfüllst: Wir sind offen für Persönlichkeiten mit Potenzial und Leidenschaft. Über uns Willkommen im trawa-Universum! Wir haben es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, das grüne Versorgungsunternehmen der Zukunft von Grund auf aufzubauen. Wie machen wir das? Wir schaffen einen direkten Zugang zu erneuerbarer Energie für B2B-Industrieunternehmen. Wir entwickeln Software und Technologie, um die Volatilität des Energiemarktes zu bewältigen. Wir professionalisieren die Energiebeschaffung auf der Käuferseite. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: (Senior) Associate – Energy Markets & Business Development (Railway Power & PPAs)
description: (Senior) Associate – Energy Markets & Business Development (Railway Power & PPAs) Our mission for you European energy costs are 2x compared to US and China. Electricity demand is expected to double by 2050. Market price volatility & complexity are here to stay. The backbone of Europe's industrial economy is at risk - and companies need to act now. trawa is building the solution: the first integrated B2B energy platform that orchestrates procurement, energy management, and flexibility steering in one product. Supply, Manage, Flex - combined. That integration unlocks up to 30% in recurring electricity cost savings - all while helping companies switch to renewable energy. We're the fastest-growing B2B energy platform in Europe. Active in Germany and Austria now, and expanding operations to a third market in 2027. We're on the road to European scale and move fast - the market window is open and we intend to own it. About trawa trawa is a scale-up based in Berlin with ~100 FTE, ~30 of whom work in Product & Tech. We've raised over €35M to date, including a €24M Series A in May 2025, backed by Balderton, Headline, Speedinvest, AENU, Magnetic, and Tiny VC. All three founders are on board and 100% committed to build the utility of the future. We're looking for a (Senior) Associate – Energy Markets & Business Development (Railway Power & PPAs) to own an important part of our energy value chain. You'll report directly to our Energy Operations Manager with close collaboration with the COO and Trading Team. You'll shape the product that makes European industry competitive again - and you'll do it at pace. This role is based in Berlin. trawa is an "office first" company, which means you will work from the office typically five days per week. The Team You'll join our Energy Operations team, which owns the energy side of our business - from sourcing and portfolio management to making sure our customers' energy products work in practice. You'll work hand in hand with our Trading Team as well as with Sales, Pricing, Product and Tech. You start without direct reports, but with a clear mandate: build and grow the business areas you own. What you'll do As (Senior) Associate – Energy Markets & Business Development, you combine a strong analytical mind with business building: Build our railway power business: A significant share of our customers comes from the railway power (Bahnstrom) segment. You take ownership of this segment from a trading and energy perspective - you understand its specific market setup, improve how we forecast, source, price and supply railway power, and make us the go-to partner for these customers. You dig into how we currently predict our railway customers' energy demand and find ways to make these forecasts more accurate. You also build partnerships with IT service providers from the railway industry and with infrastructure operators. Lead international railway expansion: You drive the expansion of our railway power offering into further European countries - you analyse market structures, regulation and commercial potential, and contribute your findings into a concrete go-to-market plan. Expand our long-term product offering: Our customers buy long-term products from us, such as PPAs and Future/Forwards products. You develop our offering so we can provide more and better-fitting products to our customers. Architect of the long-term trading process: You centralise and streamline the end-to-end process from pricing and offer creation to actual trade execution across Sales, Pricing, Trading and Operations - making it faster, more robust and scalable, and ultimately enabling a better product for our customers. Bridge between trading and business: You work closely with our quant trading and data science team and turn their models and insights into processes and systems that work across teams and markets - so that pricing, risk and market insights reliably translate into better decisions and products for our customers. Who we are looking for Strong quantitative skills: You think analytically, feel at home with numbers and data and can confidently challenge quantitative results - without having to be a quant or developer yourself. Ideally, you have a degree in a quantitative or business field (e.g. economics, engineering, industrial engineering, business administration). Business acumen & venture mindset: You think commercially, enjoy building new business areas from scratch and prioritise by impact. Interest in energy markets & trading: You are fascinated by how energy markets work - from wholesale and forward markets to PPAs, hedging and pricing - and want to dive deep into them. First exposure to these topics is a strong plus. Hungry & ambitious: You want to grow fast, take on responsibility early and set high standards for yourself. You don't wait for instructions - you find answers, push topics forward and enjoy a steep learning curve. High ownership & structured execution: You drive topics end-to-end, align stakeholders across departments and turn ideas into scalable processes with tangible business impact. Communication: You speak German at native level and very good English, and you translate confidently between commercial, quantitative and operational perspectives. 90 Day Goals After 6 Weeks (Onboarding): You have understood trawa's business, product and energy value chain in detail and got to know all relevant internal and external stakeholders. You understand our railway power customers, their contracts, how we currently forecast their energy demand and how we source, price and supply their energy. You have mapped our current long-term trading process - from pricing and offer creation to trade execution - and identified the key pain points. Month 3 (Ramp-Up): You are the go-to person for trading and energy questions in the railway power segment, have implemented first improvements and developed a concept for improving our demand forecasts for railway customers. You have delivered a first assessment of potential expansion markets for railway power, including a recommendation on which country to tackle first, and have identified and approached first potential partners among railway IT service providers and infrastructure operators. You have designed a target process for our long-term trading, started its implementation and proposed first additions to our long-term product offering. What Will Help You Succeed Work experience in a high-paced environment, e.g. a start-up, scale-up or consulting. Experience in energy markets - especially in energy trading, origination or pricing - or in financial trading markets. Knowledge of the German energy market and/or the railway power (16.7 Hz traction power) market. An affinity for AI-powered tools and automation to make processes faster and smarter. Why us? Impact: European SMEs spend between €150k and €10M per year on electricity — most are overpaying and locked into outdated procurement. Your product will directly change how thousands of companies buy, manage, and use energy. The impact is measurable, the market is massive, and the timing is now. The Role: You build business areas at the intersection of trading, energy and venture development - with direct impact on our revenue, our product offering and our expansion across Europe. Responsibility & Support: You own real business areas from day one - backed by our Energy Operations Manager, the COO and an experienced Trading Team who help you ramp up quickly and grow into the role. Ownership: We empower our team members to take ownership of their work and drive results, regardless of background or experience level. Learning & Growth: We provide an annual budget and dedicated time for professional development. You'll have opportunities for mentorship, learning, and career progression. Diversity and Inclusion: We're an equal opportunity employer, and our team reflects that. Our organisation brings together over 15 nationalities, contributing a variety of languages, experiences, and perspectives. At trawa, we're family-friendly with parents across all levels, and our diversity is represented throughout the company, including leadership. We're committed to an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work. Package & Benefits: We offer a competitive compensation package including salary and stock options, 30 days of vacation, and a range of benefits including subsidies for home internet and lunches, a Sports Club membership, dedicated learning days with an annual learning budget, plus a weekly team lunch and regular team events. At trawa, we're dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly, we encourage you to apply - you may be the right fit for this or another opportunity. raw.title: Partner Development Manager
raw.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Adoption of AI is moving rapidly from pilots to production. Enterprises and public sector organizations are investing in generative-AI programs, creating a once-in-a-decade market inflection point. At Cohere, we're committed to transforming the enterprise landscape through strategic partnerships and innovative AI solutions. As a Partner Development Manager for Germany and the DACH Region focused on the Public Sector & Enterprise Market, you'll be at the heart of our mission to empower businesses and government entities across the region with cutting-edge AI technologies.

This role is perfect for someone who thrives in a dynamic, cross-cultural environment and is passionate about driving growth through collaboration. You'll work closely with leading enterprises, system integrators, technology partners, and public sector organizations to co-create value, expand market reach, and deliver impactful AI solutions tailored to the unique needs of businesses and government agencies.

Your work will directly contribute to our success. You'll have the opportunity to shape partnerships that drive digital transformation in both commercial and public sectors, foster innovation, and position Cohere as a leader in the AI ecosystem.

If you're a strategic thinker, a relationship builder, and eager to make a meaningful impact in one of the world's most dynamic markets including the public sector, this role is your chance to shape the future of AI.

Key Responsibilities

Partner Strategy & Execution

  • Define and execute Cohere's partner go-to-market plan for the Enterprise & Public Sector Market, aligning with regional business objectives.

  • Partner with the broader GTM team to identify and recruit high-impact partners across system integrators, distributors, resellers, ISVs, cloud providers, and public sector consultancy firms.

  • Develop relationships with key stakeholders across the partner ecosystem, including government agencies, municipalities, and public sector institutions, to ensure partnership success.

Partner Onboarding & Enablement

  • Lead partner onboarding, certification, and training programs to ensure partners are equipped to sell, deploy and manage Cohere's solutions effectively for both commercial and public sector customers.

  • Collaborate with enablement to scale partner enablement through sales and technical workshops, empowering them to deliver value to enterprise customers and government agencies.

Pipeline Generation & Co-Selling

  • Own joint pipeline generation by creating co-sell motions, solution plays, and strategic joint go-to market motions that align Cohere's capabilities with enterprise mission needs and public sector procurement cycles.

  • Collaborate with partners to identify and pursue high-value opportunities in both commercial and government contracts.

Business Planning & Performance Tracking

  • Ensure partners are aligned with Cohere's strategic goals and performance metrics, including public sector compliance and reporting requirements.

  • Run joint business planning sessions and quarterly business reviews (QBRs) with partners, tracking sourced and influenced ARR against targets.

Partner Advocacy & Feedback

  • Serve as the voice of the partner within Cohere, relaying feedback to Product, Engineering, and Legal teams.

  • Work with Cohere's Public Policy teams to navigate government AI policies and regulations to advise partners on risk management and responsible AI best practices for the public sector.

Thought Leadership & Evangelism

  • Evangelize Cohere's vision and solutions at partner and industry events, positioning Cohere as a leader in responsible GenAI for both commercial and public sector markets.

  • Build thought leadership through briefings, speaking engagements, and collaborative initiatives focused on AI in government and public services.

Why You'll Love This Role

This is a high-impact role where you'll shape the future of AI partnerships in both commercial and public sectors. You'll work at the intersection of technology, business, and policy, driving growth while ensuring responsible AI adoption across enterprises and government organizations. If you're passionate about building strategic alliances, driving innovation, and making a difference in one of the world's most dynamic markets including the public sector, this is the role for you.

What We're Looking For

  • 8+ years of experience in partner development, channel sales, or alliance management within the tech industry, preferably in AI or cloud solutions, with a track record of enterprise ARR contribution and public sector partnerships.

  • Deep understanding of public sector organizations, government agencies, and municipal institutions, plus the enterprise market and key industry verticals.

  • Strong relationship-building and negotiation skills, with a track record of driving partner success in both commercial and public sector environments.

  • Experience and demonstrated depth with Sovereign Cloud GTM.

  • Ability to navigate complex regulatory and compliance landscapes, including AI ethics, government policies, and public sector procurement requirements.

  • Working understanding of AI (LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows) and their applications in enterprise and public sector contexts.

  • Experience working with major system integrators, global consultancies, hyperscalers, and public sector technology partners including joint GTM and co-sell motions.

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to evangelize Cohere's vision to partners, government stakeholders, and industry organizations.

  • Results-driven growth mindset and bias for action. You thrive in a start-up-speed environment and enjoy building and scaling partner programs across commercial and public sectors.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working in a dynamic, cross-cultural environment and wants to make a meaningful impact on how AI transforms both businesses and public services. The Berlin location provides access to a vibrant tech ecosystem with strong connections to European public sector initiatives and government partnerships.

  • A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

  • Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

  • RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

  • Annual enrichment benefits:

    Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

    Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

  • 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

  • Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

title: Junior Data Scientist

We are building the future of marketing by rewarding our community of over 95 million users for engaging with our advertisers’ products. We are offering a new way to acquire users for the biggest companies in the world. Berlin, On-site €60K – €85K + Equity Most Junior Data Scientists spend their first years building dashboards and reporting on what already happened. Here, you'll work on models that run in production and shape what millions of users see every day. You'll join a small team of people who have built and shipped ML systems at scale, and learn from them directly. You get real problems from week one, and the support to solve them. Show us you can own more, and we'll give you more. raw.title: Growth Associate (Intern)
raw.description:
Who we are

Melotech is revolutionizing media and entertainment. We create art through technology for humans to enjoy. In just 24 months, our work has been heard, watched and loved for over 4 billion minutes worldwide.

Founded by entrepreneur and investor Soheil Mirpour, we are backed by top VCs Cherry Ventures, Speedinvest and GFC, alongside world-class angels from firms such as Spotify, Blackstone and KKR.

 

What you will do

Melotech is scaling fast, and organic reach is one of the engines behind it. As Growth Associate (Intern), you help run that engine end to end: the creators, the formats, the trends and the numbers behind them. This is an organic growth role first, measured on how much reach every hour and every euro brings back. You work directly with our founders, our Growth Manager, product and data team.

Today that means a steady stream of new products that each deserve a shot at going viral across TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. Your first job is to build the machine behind that: find the creators and communities that move culture, turn what works into repeatable playbooks, and run more experiments in a week than most teams run in a quarter.

 

On a typical day, your tasks may include:

  • Creator network: finding, briefing and paying creators and pages at scale, from small accounts with loyal audiences to the ones that set trends, and keeping the ones that deliver

  • Seeding: getting our products into the formats and communities where they can travel, at the right moment and in the right volume

  • Trend spotting: catching formats and memes early and moving on them within days, not weeks

  • Experiments: running many cheap tests every week, with clear rules for what wins and what gets killed, and turning the winners into playbooks the team can repeat

  • New channels: finding places where attention is still cheap, from fan pages and communities to platforms nobody on the team is using yet

  • Organic and paid together: working with our Growth Manager so organic winners get scaled with paid, and what paid learns feeds back into organic

  • Measurement: knowing which number answers which question, for example what saves and shares tell you that views do not, and what each view really costs

  • Tooling: building the trackers, scripts and automations you need, with platform data and AI tools as your daily coworkers

 

Who you are

We're looking for a student or recent graduate who lives on the platforms and wants to learn how to make content travel.

Typically, your profile will look like this:

  • Platform fluency: you know TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts well and can explain why a post performs

  • Hands-on experience: you have grown an account, a page or a side project, or supported a startup or brand on social

  • Creator marketing: you enjoy working with creators and have a feel for content that looks native

  • Creativity: you bring fresh ideas and test them in a structured way

  • Analytical: you are comfortable with numbers and spreadsheets; SQL, Python or AI tools are a plus

  • Pace: you thrive in a fast-paced and performance-oriented environment

  • A big plus: you are a creator yourself, or have run pages with a real following

  • Academics: pursuing or recently graduated with a degree at a top-tier university, with an outstanding academic record: grades, scholarships or awards to show for it

 

What makes this exciting

You own a lever the whole company feels. Every breakout you engineer shows up directly in how fast we can grow, at a fraction of what paid reach would cost. You're not a cog in the machine but the captain of your own ship, rewarded for performance and respected for leadership. Flat hierarchies mean that your voice matters, your ideas get implemented, and your impact is immediate.

We pay competitive salaries and make you an owner of the business with equity. We work remotely to give you complete freedom over your life, while meeting regularly around the world for global offsites where we strategize, bond, and push boundaries together.

 

What the process will look like

We hire on a rolling basis. Earliest starting date is always ASAP.

Once you begin our process, you can progress from start to offer within a week, depending on how quickly you can move through each stage:

  1. Initial interview: 30-minute introductory call, getting to know you

  2. Case interview: 90-minute case discussion, present and debate your skills

  3. Founder interview: 90-minute interview with our CEO, going deep on all topics

  4. Offer, contract signing and onboarding

 

Note: As we are still in stealth, you will learn more about Melotech as you progress through the stages. By the end of the Founder interview, you will have a full grasp of our business and the details of your role.

Founded by entrepreneur and investor Soheil Mirpour, we are backed by top VCs Cherry Ventures, Speedinvest and GFC, alongside world-class angels from firms such as Spotify, Blackstone and KKR.

 

What you will do

Melotech is scaling fast, and organic reach is one of the engines behind it. As Organic Growth Lead, you own that engine end to end: the creators, the formats, the trends and the numbers behind them. This is an organic growth role first, measured on how much reach every hour and every euro brings back. You work directly with our founders, our Growth Manager, product and data team.

Today that means a steady stream of new products that each deserve a shot at going viral across TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. Your first job is to build the machine behind that: find the creators and communities that move culture, turn what works into repeatable playbooks, and run more experiments in a week than most teams run in a quarter.

 

On a typical day, your tasks may include:

  • Creator network: finding, briefing and paying creators and pages at scale, from small accounts with loyal audiences to the ones that set trends, and keeping the ones that deliver

  • Seeding: getting our products into the formats and communities where they can travel, at the right moment and in the right volume

  • Trend spotting: catching formats and memes early and moving on them within days, not weeks

  • Experiments: running many cheap tests every week, with clear rules for what wins and what gets killed, and turning the winners into playbooks the team can repeat

  • New channels: finding places where attention is still cheap, from fan pages and communities to platforms nobody on the team is using yet

  • Organic and paid together: working with our Growth Manager so organic winners get scaled with paid, and what paid learns feeds back into organic

  • Measurement: knowing which number answers which question, for example what saves and shares tell you that views do not, and what each view really costs

  • Tooling: building the trackers, scripts and automations you need, with platform data and AI tools as your daily coworkers

 

Who you are

We're looking for a hands-on organic operator who lives on the platforms, or a creative growth generalist who has made things travel. Either way, you have done it yourself, not through a team or an agency, and you can show the numbers.

Typically, your profile will look like this:

  • Interest: a strong interest in organic growth, creator marketing and social, ideally with hands-on experience from a startup, brand, app, creator agency or your own channels

  • Breakouts you can show: you have made things go viral more than once, for a brand, an app or your own channels, and you can explain why it worked and what it cost

  • Creator marketing at scale: you have run creator or UGC programs with many creators at once, negotiated the rates and written briefs that keep the content native; ideally you bring a network of creators, pages and managers

  • Platform fluency: you know how TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts distribute content today, what makes a hook, and when a format is burning out

  • Creativity with discipline: you come up with ideas nobody else would try, and then test them properly, with small budgets, kill rules and numbers

  • Measurement: you track reach, engagement and cost per view in your own data, not in screenshots, and you judge every channel by what it brings back

  • Data and tooling: you are fast in spreadsheets, ideally comfortable with SQL or Python, and you automate the boring parts with AI tools

  • Pace: you thrive in a fast-paced and performance-oriented environment

  • A big plus: you are or were a creator yourself, or have run pages with a real following, and you're into media, entertainment, gaming or social

 

What makes this exciting

You own a lever the whole company feels. Every breakout you engineer shows up directly in how fast we can grow, at a fraction of what paid reach would cost. You're not a cog in the machine but the captain of your own ship, rewarded for performance and respected for leadership. Flat hierarchies mean that your voice matters, your ideas get implemented, and your impact is immediate.

We pay competitive salaries and make you an owner of the business with equity. We work remotely to give you complete freedom over your life, while meeting regularly around the world for global offsites where we strategize, bond, and push boundaries together.

 

What the process will look like

We hire on a rolling basis. Earliest starting date is always ASAP.

Once you begin our process, you can progress from start to offer within a week, depending on how quickly you can move through each stage:

  1. Initial interview: 30-minute introductory call, getting to know you

  2. Case interview: 90-minute case discussion, present and debate your skills

  3. Founder interview: 90-minute interview with our CEO, going deep on all topics

  4. Offer, contract signing and onboarding

 

Note: As we are still in stealth, you will learn more about Melotech as you progress through the stages. By the end of the Founder interview, you will have a full grasp of our business and the details of your role.

raw.description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our ADAS Team

Wayve's ADAS engineering teams build the perception and intelligence that power driver assistance in real-world driving. We work end-to-end, from creating high-quality training data, to developing and evaluating CV/3D perception models, to iterating quickly based on performance gaps. The team mixes "online" (on-car, latency/compute constrained) and "offline" (heavier, large-scale data generation) work, with a strong focus on measurable impact and shipping.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Train, debug, and improve computer vision and 3D perception models, iterating based on clear evaluation signals

  • Work across the full ML lifecycle: data, training, evaluation, and iteration

  • Partner with the team to decide what to tackle next, based on where the system is underperforming

  • Build scalable data pipelines, including auto-labelling and pseudo-labelling, to accelerate model development

     

🧩 What you'll be working on:

  • Core ADAS perception capabilities such as detection, classification, and instance segmentation, spanning lanes, objects, traffic signs, and traffic lights

  • End-to-end approaches that let the model act on the world directly, rather than relying on a chain of hand-coded intermediate steps (lane assist without ever explicitly detecting lane lines is the kind of outcome we're after)

  • Online perception that runs fast in-car as part of our production stack

  • Offline perception work using additional inputs not viable for on-road production, including extra sensors like lidar, future frames, maps, and extra compute, to improve data quality and coverage at scale

  • Building the "data flywheel": using offline models and 3D tracking/reconstruction to auto-generate labels and accelerate iteration across perception tasks

     

👤 You should apply if:

  • Built and shipped CV-focused deep learning systems, with strong applied ML engineering rather than research-only work

  • Experience with 3D perception concepts or pipelines, such as LiDAR, multi-view geometry, tracking, or 3D reconstruction

  • Comfortable owning work end-to-end, including evaluation and large-scale dataset generation

  • Enjoy pragmatic problem-solving under real product constraints

  • Excited to improve real-world driving performance through better perception

  • Automotive domain experience is a bonus, but not a blocker if your perception background comes from elsewhere

🌱 Not ticking every box? That's totally okay! If you're passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚗 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve's mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻 — Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

📋 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

  • Competency interviews (programming and system design; 2 hours)

  • Deep-dive technical interviews (Hiring manager/Domain Interview; 1 hour)

  • Final interview: mission & values alignment (1 hour)

We'll always explain the format and work around your availability.

 

What's in it for you (Location dependent):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partner discounts and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

title: Senior Manager, Credit Risk
description: About Airwallex Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own. We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full. About the team The Credit Risk team is part of Airwallex’s Second Line of Defence and helps the company grow responsibly as a global financial platform. We work at the intersection of credit, FX, and counterparty risk, partnering closely with Product, Sales, Operations, Treasury, Finance, Engineering, Compliance, and Legal to enable commercial growth while protecting Airwallex from financial loss and excessive risk exposure. This is a team for analytical, commercially minded risk leaders who are energized by building scalable frameworks and practical controls across a fast-moving, multi-currency global network. What you'll do As a Senior Manager, Credit Risk, you will lead Airwallex's global second-line oversight of credit, FX, and counterparty risk. You will set the risk guardrails that allow the business to grow safely across merchant acquiring, charge cards, FX, treasury, settlement, and banking-partner activities. Reporting to the Senior Director, Financial Risk, you will own the global framework, risk appetite, limits, governance, and portfolio oversight for these risk areas. You will provide independent challenge to first-line decisions and act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders across the business. This role is based in London. Responsibilities Credit risk framework and risk appetite: Define, implement, and continuously enhance the global second-line credit risk framework, including policies, risk appetite thresholds, limits, escalation protocols, and governance standards across Airwallex’s products and legal entities. Credit portfolio oversight: Oversee credit exposures across merchant acquiring, charge cards, B2B and commercial activities, FX pre-funding, treasury-related exposures, settlement flows, and other relevant products. Underwriting and limit governance: Review and challenge first-line underwriting strategies, customer and merchant risk policies, credit assessments, limit-setting methodologies, and exception processes. Act as a senior escalation point for complex or high-value credit decisions. FX risk oversight: Establish and monitor appropriate second-line guardrails for FX exposures arising from pre-funding, settlement, customer activity, treasury flows, and other multi-currency activities. Challenge controls, limits, escalation triggers, and risk reporting to ensure exposures remain within approved tolerances. Counterparty risk management: Set and oversee counterparty risk standards for banking partners, payment partners, merchants, customers, and other material counterparties. Establish appropriate exposure limits, concentration thresholds, monitoring requirements, and escalation processes. Portfolio monitoring and early warning indicators: Lead proactive monitoring of credit, FX, and counterparty portfolios, including exposure, concentration, delinquency, default, chargeback, loss, settlement, liquidity-of-counterparty, and other relevant risk indicators. Identify emerging trends and escalate material issues before they become systemic. Loss mitigation and remediation: Review and challenge first-line monitoring, collections, collateral, prefunding, reserves, chargeback, and other mitigation strategies. Ensure deteriorating counterparties, customers, merchants, or exposures are identified and addressed promptly. New products and market expansion: Partner with Product, Engineering, Commercial, Treasury, Finance, and Operations to assess and challenge the risk design of new products, features, markets, currencies, and partner arrangements before launch. Risk approvals and governance: Lead or support risk committee decisions, material risk approvals, limit exceptions, breach assessments, and remediation plans. Ensure decisions are documented clearly and aligned with approved risk appetite. Regulatory and partner engagement: Represent Credit Risk during regulatory examinations, internal and external audits, and reviews with banking and strategic partners. Prepare clear, decision-useful materials for senior management, risk committees, and the Board where appropriate. Who you are We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory. Minimum qualifications 10–15 years of progressively senior experience across credit risk, counterparty risk, FX risk, treasury risk, or related financial risk disciplines within banking, payments, fintech, or another highly regulated financial services environment. Deep experience designing, implementing, and governing second-line credit risk frameworks in a complex, multi-jurisdictional organization. Strong understanding of credit risk identification, measurement, underwriting, limit management, monitoring, mitigation, provisioning, loss recognition, and capital implications. Demonstrated experience managing risk across multiple product lines, such as merchant acquiring, commercial or charge cards, B2B lending, payment processing, FX, treasury, settlement, or banking-partner activities. Practical experience overseeing FX and counterparty risk, including exposure measurement, concentration risk, limits, settlement risk, prefunding, collateral or other mitigants, and escalation governance. Proven ability to challenge first-line decisions and communicate clear risk positions to senior executives, commercial leaders, product and operations teams, banking partners, auditors, and regulators. Preferred qualifications Advanced degree such as an MBA or Master's in Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or a related field. Professional certification such as FRM, PRM, CFA, or an equivalent qualification. Experience with automated decisioning engines, credit scoring models, portfolio analytics, or alternative data used in underwriting and monitoring. Familiarity with IFRS 9, expected credit loss methodologies, stress testing, or other relevant prudential and accounting frameworks. Strong data literacy and familiarity with SQL, Python, or similar tools used to analyze portfolio, exposure, and loss trends. Experience working in a regulated payments fintech, digital bank, or financial institution with multiple licenses and banking partnerships. Comfort operating in a high-growth environment with evolving priorities and a bias for practical, scalable execution. Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @ airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page. Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary. Equal opportunity Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

You report to the Operating Partner, but work directly and independently with every member of the firm.

We believe different viewpoints drive our growth, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

What you'll own

The data platform. The firm's data architecture end to end: warehouse, ingestion from core systems (CRM, meeting transcripts, documents, email/calendar), entity resolution, and data quality. One person, one company, one deal – consistent across every source. This is foundational; everything else flows from it.

The intelligence layer. Retrieval, search & agent tooling that give everyone's AI real firm context, serving both individual workflows (bottom-up) and firm-wide platforms (top-down). Built for passive compounding: the system gets better as people work and as models improve, without depending on anyone's discipline.

Access, trust, and AI risk. The access model as structural enforcement, not instructions: who sees what, with identity, provenance, and audit. Sensitive fund and partner data protected to a standard the partnership will trust, plus the AI-specific risk judgment (injection containment, egress, tool guardrails) for everything the function ships, in collaboration with legal/regulatory counsel.

Technology strategy and the tool estate. Accountability for whether the firm's tools are the right ones: evaluation, integration, and replacement of the systems and data sources the firm runs on, in close partnership with the stakeholders who use them. Buy when buying is better; build when building is better. You have the mandate to choose, and then execute on your decision. Make sure security, compliance and budget are part of the equation.

What you'll deliver

First 6 months. A complete map of the firm's data and systems. The foundational data platform stood up. Two or three lightweight tools shipped that visibly improve how a team works. A clear, prioritized 12–18 month roadmap, authored by you and agreed with the partnership.

By 12 months. V1 of the firm's shared intelligence layer live and in daily use. The diligence process made genuinely multiplayer; firm knowledge and meeting history informing live deals instead of sitting unused. Measurable adoption, reported honestly, with failures killed as quickly as the wins are shipped.

Beyond. The roadmap is yours to define. Candidates for the frontier: productizing how the firm wins deals, network intelligence that answers "who do we know" in seconds, platform tools founders can self-serve, and operational automation across finance, events, and admin.

How you'll work

  • Builder first. You ship personally. This is not a role for someone who wants a team of ten doing the building.

  • Co-creation, not solo genius. Stakeholders across the firm (investment, platform, marketing, operations, etc.) steer, test, and tune what you build. Within a year, everyone at the firm should be able to point at something they had a hand in shaping.

  • Product discipline. Prototype, validate with real users, kill what doesn't get adopted. Usage is the metric; expect and budget for churn.

  • Scale deliberately. You start solo. As the foundation proves out, you'll orchestrate internal or external build resources and potentially grow the function. You are prepared to identify, leverage and lead exceptional talent to help achieve results.

Who you are

  • You've shipped a real data or AI product end to end (pipelines, retrieval, and the product surface) and people actually used it.

  • Deep, hands-on command of data architecture, warehousing, and governance. Fluent with embeddings, retrieval, and agents that act, not just answer.

  • You treat access control and provenance as product features, not compliance chores.

  • Low ego, high agency, energized by a blank page. Excited to tackle the unglamorous work (entity resolution, data hygiene, permissions) that everything depends on.

  • You can sit with an investor, an EA, and a founder in the same week and design for all of them. Venture experience isn't required, but you'll need to earn a front-line view of the work fast.

  • Not IT operations: endpoint, device & office infrastructure are handled by our managed IT partner.

  • Not reg compliance: policy & DORA workstreams are owned by legal, with your input on anything AI.

  • Not a reporting function: you build systems that answer questions, not dashboards on request.

You'll have a blank page, real budget influence, direct partnership access, and a firm small enough that what you build touches everyone within weeks. The firms that figure this out will compound differently from the ones that don't. This is the seat where that happens.

This role is not a good fit for you if: You’re not motivated by customer-facing work or influencing customer outcomes through proactive engagement and collaboration. title: Commercial Specialist
description: Powering Great Work We started as the place to find a trusted trade. Now, as we shape the future of home improvement, we're building the tech to transform that landscape for everyone - better products, smarter data, AI where it actually helps - so trades can spend less time on admin and consumers can find someone they trust, first time. That's Powering Great Work, and it's why every team here exists: 🔧 Trades spend less time on admin and more on winning work and growing their business 🏠 Homeowners get a trusted trade, first time, every time 🚀 We get to build products that change homes and lives across the country As our next Account Executive, you'll help bring more trades onto Checkatrade across different regions and categories. It's a new business role: you find high-potential trade businesses and guide them from the first conversation to a signed deal. You'll sit in our Strategic Growth team, at the heart of how we grow the trade network that homeowners rely on. The job, unfiltered: Win new trade businesses by finding high-potential small and medium trades, building proposals that make sense for them and negotiating terms. Hand each new trade over smoothly to our vetting team, so the start of their Checkatrade journey goes well. Spot opportunities in the market, using data and insights to see where Checkatrade is strong and where we can grow. Work with Account Management, Vetting, Product and Operations to find the regions and categories that would benefit most from Checkatrade. Learn our product suite inside out, so every business case is tailored to the prospect in front of you. Own the outbound sales cycle, from prospecting and qualification through to proposals, negotiation and closing. The fit: Solid experience in commercial or new business sales, ideally in similar markets, with a strong focus on outbound acquisition. A track record of finding new clients, building tailored proposals and hitting revenue targets. Each of our HSCs handle over 40 million parcels annually, with our largest site measuring more than 300,000 sq ft.

You will also be accountable for whether the site is measurably better in a month than it is today for each of our key metrics. You are on the floor for your shift, every shift. This is not a project role with occasional site visits and it is not a desk job, the forward work happens along with running the operation.

 

Who will thrive in this role

  • Deliver shift plan end to end people deployment, throughput, quality standards, and health & safety compliance

  • Lead, develop, and performance-manage a frontline team of 50–100+ operatives

  • Build the mechanisms that hold the operation together. Build controls, cadences, metrics, SOPs, change management and own their adoption, not only their design

  • Plan ahead for future shifts; labour, training, and the risks you can see coming before they land

  • Own the end-of-shift handover; what happened, what is at risk, what the next shift needs to know

  • Stay decisive through volume peaks, outages, and labour gaps. Triage, solve the problem at hand quickly, contain the impact, restore flow

  • Present and write clearly whether briefs, escalations, handovers or post-incident reviews. Decisions here get made based off what you wrote

  • Implement changes into a live operation such as introducing robotics, launching new sortation tech or onboarding new clients. We are changing the operations constantly which means you’ll roll change out mid flight and bring your team along the journey.

 

Who you are

  • Scaled something from zero: a site, a market, a process or a program.

  • Managed a physical operation: quick commerce, grocery, e-commerce fulfillment, last mile, 3PL, food production, airport ground handling, rail. Anywhere with a hard cut off and people on the floor.

  • Communicate in both directions and have strong people management skills: you can brief 80 operatives at shift start and take a problem to senior leadership the same day.

  • Built a mechanism that held: a control, a cadence, a metric, a document standard. Something you authored that changed how frontline teams worked.

  • Own numbers rather than report them: you can name a metric you created or redefined, explain why the previous one was wrong, and say what changed afterwards.

  • Understand frontline work: one of these must be true: you have personally led frontline teams; you have worked embedded in and around a frontline population day to day, without the reporting line; or you have been accountable for outcomes delivered by frontline people you did not employ.

You do not need to have worked in parcels, fulfilment, or sortation. Several of our most talented people had not.

 

Backgrounds that translate well

  • Program Manager in a logistics or e-commerce business

  • Operations Excellence and Continuous Improvement

  • Strategy & Operations

  • Transformation manager

  • Launch and Expansion Manager

  • Regional operations manager

We have hired well from corporate operations, from central operations inside large UK retailers and carriers, and from quick commerce and marketplace operators.   • Final interview (45 min). Decision and offer within 48 hours

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.
